rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem treats the wise person's poverty and the fool's comfortable life as evidence for divine decree.
rows.anchor: ومن الدليل على القضاء وكونه … بؤس اللبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kingship includes every kind of sovereignty: prophethood, knowledge, intellect, health, good character, power, love, and wealth; the wording is general and cannot be restricted without evidence.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن قوله { تؤتى الملك من تشاء } محمول على جميع أنواع الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honor can be religious or worldly; faith is the highest religious honor, as 63:8 says that glory belongs to God, His Messenger, and believers.
rows.anchor: أما في الدين فأشرف أنواع العزة الإيمان قال الله تعالى : { ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because faith is the greatest honor and unbelief the greatest abasement, their creation cannot be credited to human choice: otherwise people would honor or abase themselves more than God does.
rows.anchor: فعلمنا أن الإعزاز بالإيمان والحق ليس إلا من الله ، والإذلال بالكفر والباطل ليس إلا من الله

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says religious honor includes reward with glorification and praise, added divine favors, and superiority over enemies; worldly honor includes wealth, abundant crops and livestock, and awe in people's hearts.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : الإعزاز المضاف إليه تعالى قد يكون في الدين ، وقد يكون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues against al-Qadi that if reward's glorification is obligatory for God, the believer who chose faith would earn greater honor for himself than God gives him.
rows.anchor: كل ما يفعله الله تعالى من التعظيم في باب الثواب فهو حق واجب على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says God humiliates enemies alone; poverty, illness, or dependence afflicting His friends lead to afterlife honor or compensation, like painful cupping that brings great benefit, and poverty is only figuratively called abasement as in 5:54.
rows.anchor: فقال الجبائي في ( تفسيره ) : إنه تعالى إنما يذل أعداءه في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites say God humiliates opponents through blame and curse, withholding proof and victory, subjecting them to believers and making their wealth spoils, and punishing them in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: لهم في الآخرة هذا جملة كلام المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's doctrine is that God honors some through faith and knowledge and humiliates others through unbelief and misguidance; these are the greatest forms of honor and abasement.
rows.anchor: ومذهبنا أنه تعالى يعز البعض بالإيمان والمعرفة ، ويذل البعض بالكفر والضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First argument: the agent of Islam's honor and unbelief's abasement is either the servant or God; people want faith and guidance, so when ignorance occurs instead, its source is God.
rows.anchor: فلما أراد العبد الإيمان ولم يحصل له بل حصل له الجهل ، علمنا أن حصوله من الله تعالى لا من العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second argument: ignorance cannot always arise from an earlier doubt or ignorance without an impossible regress, and rational people do not choose ignorance spontaneously; God therefore abandons them to it.
rows.anchor: لكنا نجد من أنفسنا أن العاقل لا يرضى لنفسه أن يصير على الجهل ابتداء من غير موجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third argument: every act requires a motive or determining cause from God; when it leads toward good it is honor, and when toward ignorance and misguidance it is abasement.
rows.anchor: وذلك المرجح يكون من الله تعالى فإن كان في طرف الخير كان إعزازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hand means power; the definite article in good makes the phrase general, so God's power brings about every blessing and good.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أن المراد من اليد هو القدرة ، والمعنى بقدرتك الخير والألف واللام في الخير يوجبان العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase also restricts all good to God, as 109:6 restricts each community to its own religion; all good therefore comes from God's creation and origination.
rows.anchor: فثبت دلالة هذه الآية من هذين الوجهين على أن جميع الخيرات منه ، وبتكوينه وتخليقه وإيجاده وإبداعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since faith and knowledge of God are the best good, they too must be created by God rather than by the servant.
rows.anchor: أفضل الخيرات هو الإيمان بالله تعالى ومعرفته ، فوجب أن يكون الخير من تخليق الله تعالى لا من تخليق العبد

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: Some of Razi's companions add that if faith were the servant's creation, the servant would surpass God in goodness and perfection, an impious conclusion.
rows.anchor: ومن الأصحاب من زاد في هذا التقدير فقال : كل فاعلين فعل أحدهما أشرف وأفضل من فعل الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says that if all good is in God's hand, evil and disobedience cannot be created by Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن لا يكون الكفر والمعصية واقعين بتخليق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that the phrase denies good being in another's hand, but does not deny God also holding what is other than good; good is singled out because it benefits.
rows.anchor: وهذا ينافي أن يكون بيد غيره ولكن لا ينافي أن يكون بيده الخير وبيده ما سوى الخير

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says human good is attributable to God because He empowers and guides people to it; Razi rejects this as weak because it leaves some good, including the noblest, attributable to servants against the verse.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : كل خير حصل من جهة العباد فلولا أنه تعالى أقدرهم عليه وهداهم إليه لما تمكنوا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power over everything reinforces the preceding claims that He gives and removes sovereignty and honors or humiliates whom He wills.
rows.anchor: أما قوله { إنك على كل شىء قدير } فهذا كالتأكيد لما تقدم من كونه مالكا لإيتاء الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of God bringing night into day is that He shortens one and adds the removed time to the other; Razi says this is closer to the wording and sustains the world's order.
rows.anchor: أن يجعل الليل قصيرا ويجعل ذلك القدر الزائد داخلا في النهار وتارة على العكس من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading is that God brings each after the other, clothing the world in darkness after daylight and in light after night.
rows.anchor: أن المراد هو أنه تعالى يأتي بالليل عقيب النهار ، فيلبس الدنيا ظلمة بعد أن كان فيها ضوء النهار

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Nafi', Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read al-mayyit with a doubled y; the remaining readers lighten it, and the two forms usually have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وحمزة والكسائي { الميت } بالتشديد ، والباقون بالتخفيف ، وهما لغتان بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: المبرد والبصريون
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the Basrans unanimously treat the two forms as equivalent, citing the line that the truly dead are the living dead; some others distinguish one who has died from one who has not.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد : أجمع البصريون على أنهما سواء وأنشدوا : إنما الميت ميت الأحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that God brings a believer from an unbeliever, as Abraham from Azar, and an unbeliever from a believer, as Canaan from Noah.
rows.anchor: يخرج المؤمن من الكافر كإبراهيم من آزر ، والكافر من المؤمن مثل كنعان من نوح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators also interpret the phrase as bringing the good out of the bad and the bad out of the good.
rows.anchor: يخرج الطيب من الخبيث وبالعكس

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators also cite living creatures emerging from sperm and birds from eggs, and the reverse.
rows.anchor: يخرج الحيوان من النطفة ، والطير من البيضة وبالعكس

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators also cite a grain stalk from a seed and a date palm from a kernel, and the reverse.
rows.anchor: يخرج السنبلة من الحبة وبالعكس ، والنخلة من النواة وبالعكس

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says all these meanings are possible; the Qur'an calls guidance from unbelief life (6:122), vegetation after dead land life (30:19; 35:9), and people dead then revived (2:28).
rows.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : والكلمة محتملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After presenting proofs to Najran's Christians, who declined mutual imprecation and accepted the subordinate status of jizya, the Prophet eager for their faith is directed from polemic to a fair invitation recognized by sound reason and nature.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أورد على نصارى نجران أنواع الدلائل وانقطعوا ، ثم دعاهم إلى المباهلة فخافوا وما شرعوا فيها وقبلوا الصغار بأداء الجزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to an equitable word invites mutual fairness without either side favoring itself, leaving disputation and seeking a fair hearing.
rows.anchor: هلموا إلى كلمة فيها إنصاف من بعضنا لبعض ، ولا ميل فيه لأحد على صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported scope of People of the Book is the Christians of Najran.
rows.anchor: المراد نصارى نجران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reported scope is the Jews of Medina.
rows.anchor: المراد يهود المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view says the verse concerns both groups because the wording encompasses them and a reported occasion of revelation names Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: أنها نزلت في الفريقين ، ويدل عليه وجهان الأول : أن ظاهر اللفظ يتناولهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An occasion report says Jews objected that Muhammad wanted them to treat him as Christians treated Jesus, while Christians said he wanted them to say of him what Jews said about Uzayr.
rows.anchor: روي في سبب النزول ، أن اليهود قالوا للنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام ، ما تريد إلا أن نتخذك ربا كما اتخذت النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi favors the Christians of Najran because the discourse has just moved from proofs to imprecation and now shifts to fairness; calling them People of the Book honors and soothes them as debate gives way to fair inquiry.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن الأقرب حمله على النصارى ، لما بينا أنه لما أورد الدلائل عليهم أولا ، ثم باهلهم ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'ālaw originally meant rising from a low place to a high one, but came to mean turning toward the matter or place to which one is summoned, without physical movement.
rows.anchor: فالمراد تعيين ما دعوا إليه والتوجه إلى النظر فيه وإن لم يكن انتقالا من مكان إلى مكان لأن أصل اللفظ مأخوذ من التعالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ means justice and fairness: fairness gives each side half, avoiding wrong to oneself and others, creating equality and balance; taking more than one gives destroys that balance.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى هلموا إلى كلمة فيها إنصاف من بعضنا لبعض ، لا ميل فيه لأحد على صاحبه ، والسواء هو العدل والإنصاف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses sawāʾ as an adjective of kalima, meaning a word possessing equality: just, upright, and even, so both sides become equal and upright by accepting it.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج { سوآء } نعت للكملة يريد : ذات سواء ، فعلى هذا قوله { كلمة سواء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause an lā naʿbuda can be nominative through an omitted subject, answering what the word is: it is that we worship only God.
rows.anchor: الأول : إنه رفع بإضمار ، هي : كأن قائلا قال : ما تلك الكلمة ؟ فقيل هي أن لا نعبد إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an lā naʿbuda is genitive as an appositive to kalima.
rows.anchor: والثاني : خفض على البدل من : كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three prohibitions answer the Christians' practices: worshipping Christ, associating partners through the three persons they claim are eternal, and treating clergy as lords.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر هذه الثلاثة لأن النصارى جمعوا بين هذه الثلاثة فيعبدون غير الله وهو المسيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains that Christians describe three eternal persons as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, with the Word and Holy Spirit hypostases incarnated in Jesus and Mary.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يقولون إنه ثلاثة : أب وابن وروح القدس ، فأثبتوا ذوات ثلاثة قديمة سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reasons that if the hypostases were not independent they could not separate from the Father's essence and incarnate separately; their independence makes the three-person doctrine shirk.
rows.anchor: ولولا كون هذين الأقنومين ذاتين مستقلتين وإلا لما جازت عليهما مفارقة ذات الأب والتدرع بناسوت عيسى ومريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of taking clergy as lords is that Christians obeyed them in declaring things lawful or forbidden.
rows.anchor: أحدها : إنهم كانوا يطيعونهم في التحليل والتحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that they prostrated to their clergy.
rows.anchor: والثاني : إنهم كانوا يسجدون لأحبارهم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says their ascetics believed divine indwelling appeared in spiritually perfected people, granting powers such as reviving the dead and curing congenital blindness and leprosy; thus they affirmed lordship without using its title.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : من مذهبهم أن من صار كاملا في الرياضة والمجاهدة يظهر فيه أثر حلول اللاهوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth explanation is that they obeyed clergy in sinful acts, which is itself lordship; the Qur'an similarly describes taking desire as a deity (45:23).
rows.anchor: والرابع : هو أنهم كانوا يطيعون أحبارهم في المعاصي ، ولا معنى للربوبية إلا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues these practices are invalid: worship was directed only to God before Jesus and should remain so; shirk is universally false; and obedience in law and conduct belongs to the Creator and Benefactor, not clergy.
rows.anchor: وكان القول ببطلان هذه الأمور الثلاثة كالأمر المتفق عليه بين جمهور العقلاء وذلك ، لأن قبل المسيح ما كان المعبود إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they refuse, Muslims should publicly maintain their own submission to God rather than remain preoccupied with forcing others to adopt it.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إن أبوا إلا الإصرار ، فقولوا إنا مسلمون ، يعني أظهروا أنكم على هذا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects al-Ka'bi's first argument because the answer must match the question: the people claimed their conduct was God's ruling revealed in scripture, not that God created their alterations; the second argument therefore also fails.
rows.anchor: أما الوجه الأول : من الوجهين اللذين ذكرهما الكعبي فجوابه ، أن الجواب لا بد وأن يكون منطبقا على السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that they lie about God while knowing means they deliberately tell the lie with full awareness.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنهم يتعمدون ذلك الكذب مع العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If scriptural distortion means changing Torah wording or grammatical endings, only a small group could collude; if it means obscuring proofs of Muhammad's prophethood by doubts, a large-scale conspiracy is possible.
rows.anchor: إن كان المراد من التحريف تغيير ألفاظ التوراة ، وإعراب ألفاظها ، فالمقدمون عليه يجب أن يكونوا طائفة يسيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing scriptural scholars' distortion, Razi says one altered claim was that Jesus asserted divinity and commanded people to worship him; the verse refutes that charge.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما بين أن عادة علماء أهل الكتاب التحريف والتبديل أتبعه بما يدل على أن من جملة ما حرفوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed after Jews called Uzayr God's son and Christians called Christ God's son.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لما قالت اليهود عزير ابن الله ، وقالت النصارى : المسيح ابن الله نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An occasion report says Abu Rafi al-Qurazi and the head of the Najran delegation asked whether Muhammad wanted them to worship and take him as lord; he replied that he was sent neither to worship another nor to command other than God's worship.
rows.anchor: قيل إن أبا رافع القرظي من اليهود ورئيس وفد نجران من النصارى قالا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : أتريد أن نعبدك ونتخذك ربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another occasion report says a man asked whether they might prostrate to the Prophet; he forbade anyone prostrating to another besides God and directed them to honor the Prophet and give each his due.
rows.anchor: قال رجل يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض ، أفلا نسجد لك ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the wording can address Jews who claimed no one reached their excellence: instead of enslaving people, they should direct them to obey God and acknowledge Muhammad's prophethood as his miracles require; 9:31 offers a parallel.
rows.anchor: إن اليهود لما ادعوا أن أحدا لا ينال من درجات الفضل والمنزلة ما نالوه ، فالله تعالى قال لهم

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm reads the verse as saying that if prophets wanted to make this claim, the proof would prevent them, as 69:44–45 and 17:74–75 warn of punishment for fabricating revelation or nearly inclining to opponents.
rows.anchor: قال الأصم : معناه ، أنهم لو أرادوا أن يقولوا ذلك لمنعهم الدليل عليه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is that prophets' divinely chosen pure souls, complete knowledge, and purified character are incompatible with claiming divinity; scripture cites God's knowing where to place His message, choosing Israel knowingly, and selecting messengers (6:124; 44:32; 22:75).
rows.anchor: أن الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام موصوفون بصفات لا يحسن مع تلك الصفات ادعاء الإلاهية والربوبية منها أن الله تعالى آتاهم الكتاب والوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that God grants prophethood only when He knows the recipient will not say this.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى لا يشرف عبده بالنبوة والرسالة إلا إذا علم منه أنه لا يقول مثل هذا الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation is that if a messenger who claims to transmit God's rulings ordered worship of himself, his miracles would cease to prove his truth.
rows.anchor: فلو أمرهم بعبادة نفسه فحينئذ تبطل دلالة المعجزة على كونه صادقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the verse denies that a human granted scripture, judgment, and prophethood would make this claim; it does not merely prohibit speech already forbidden to everyone, which would not refute the charge against Jesus.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه ليس المراد من قوله { ما كان لبشر } ذلك أنه يحرم عليه هذا الكلام لأن ذلك محرم على كل الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording instead negates the claim, as 19:35 negates God taking a son and 3:161 negates a prophet committing fraud rather than merely forbidding those acts.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { ما كان الله * أن يتخذ من ولد } ( مريم : 35 ) على سبيل النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order is apt: the heavenly book is revealed first, the prophet then understands it through judgment (which linguists and exegetes identify as knowledge), and finally conveys it to people through prophethood.
rows.anchor: لأن الكتاب السماوي ينزل أولا ثم إنه يحصل في عقل النبي فهم ذلك الكتاب وإليه الإشارة بالحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading puts the verb after thumma in the subjunctive, indicating that prophethood and telling people to worship the prophet cannot coexist; it is governed by an implied an and coordinated with what came before.
rows.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة ، ثم يقول بنصب اللام

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr's reported indicative reading begins a new sentence.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو برفعها ، أما النصب فعلى تقدير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says ʿibādan is the Muzayna dialect word for slaves.
rows.anchor: حكى الواحدي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال في قوله تعالى : { كونوا عبادا لى } إنه لغة مزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase but become godly has an omitted verb, meaning but he says to them; Arabic permits such ellipsis when context makes it clear, as in 3:106.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية إضمار ، والتقدير : ولكن يقول لهم كونوا ربانيين فأضمر القول على حسب مذهب العرب
